blocks.h2: Worked example: a Linux host sends an HTTPS request
paras: This is an outbound data path , not a historical timeline. The network card does not directly understand an HTTPS URL. The operating system and applications perform different jobs.
Purpose: browser resolves a hostname and prepares a request.
Example: a browser opens an HTTPS website; DNS returns an IP address.
Purpose: TCP establishes a connection and TLS protects application traffic in a typical HTTPS-over-TCP exchange. HTTP/3 instead uses QUIC over UDP.
Example: encrypted HTTP request data is prepared for transmission.
Purpose: selects routes and interfaces; handles IP and transport processing.
Example: the kernel chooses the default route when needed.
Purpose: configures NIC transmit descriptors and device queues.
Example: a driver submits a packet buffer for transmission.
Purpose: NIC sends link-layer frames through its physical or virtual interface.
Example: Ethernet frames travel to a local switch.
Purpose: switches and routers forward traffic toward its destination; the remote server responds.
Example: a website returns an HTML response.

Arrow semantics: each step passes or prepares data for the next processing layer. The real network stack is bidirectional and contains additional details such as ARP/neighbor discovery, MTU, offloads and retransmissions.
